drivingQuestion: Is one who repeats 'Shema' silenced like one who repeats 'modim', and how does that square with the baraita that calls repeating Shema merely reprehensible?
outcomeNote: R' Zeira's ruling is upheld by distinguishing word-repetition (reprehensible) from verse-repetition (silenced); Rav Pappa's alternative (initial lack of intent) is rebuffed by Abaye.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר ״שְׁמַע שְׁמַע״ — כְּאוֹמֵר ״מוֹדִים מוֹדִים״ דָּמֵי.
segments.en: «Rabbi Zeira said: One who» repeats himself while reciting Shema and «says: Listen» Israel, «Listen» Israel «is like one who says: We give thanks, we give thanks.»

segments.he: מֵיתִיבִי: הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת שְׁמַע וְכוֹפְלָהּ — הֲרֵי זֶה מְגוּנֶּה. מְגוּנֶּה הוּא דְּהָוֵי, שַׁתּוֹקֵי לָא מְשַׁתְּקִינַן לֵיהּ!
segments.en: The Gemara «raises an objection:» It was taught in a baraita: «One who recites Shema and repeats it, it is reprehensible.» One may infer: «It is reprehensible, but they do not silence him.»

segments.he: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא, דְּאָמַר מִילְּתָא מִילְּתָא וְתָנֵי לַהּ. וְהָא, דְּאָמַר פְּסוּקָא פְּסוּקָא וְתָנֵי לֵיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «This is not difficult; this» case, where although it is reprehensible when one repeats Shema, they do not silence him, is referring to «one who recites and repeats each individual word» as he says it. In so doing he ruins the recitation of Shema. However, «this» case, where Rabbi Zeira holds that one who repeats Shema they silence him, refers to «one who recites and repeats an entire verse,» as it appears that he is worshiping separate authorities.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: וְדִילְמָא מֵעִיקָּרָא לָא כַּוֵּון דַּעְתֵּיהּ, וּלְבַסּוֹף כַּוֵּון דַּעְתֵּיהּ?
segments.en: «Rav Pappa said to Abaye» with regard to this halakha: «And perhaps initially he did not focus his attention» on the recitation of Shema, so he repeated it «and ultimately he focused his attention» as he recited it the second time?

segments.he: חַבְרוּתָא כְּלַפֵּי שְׁמַיָּא מִי אִיכָּא?! אִי לָא כַּוֵּון דַּעְתֵּיהּ מֵעִיקָּרָא — מָחֵינַן לֵיהּ בְּמַרְזַפְתָּא דְנַפָּחָא עַד דִּמְכַוֵּין דַּעְתֵּיהּ.
segments.en: «Can one have» that degree of «familiarity with Heaven,» to the extent that he can take his words lightly and say them however he likes? «If he did not focus his attention initially, we beat him with a blacksmith’s hammer until he focuses his attention,» as conduct of that sort is unacceptable.

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי זירא: כל האומר ״שמע שמע״
moves.summary: R' Zeira: repeating 'Shema' is like repeating 'modim' — he is silenced
moves.about: extends the mishna's silencing of one who says 'modim, modim' to one who repeats 'Shema'

moves.summary: objects from the baraita: one who repeats Shema is reprehensible
moves.about: the baraita calls repeating Shema merely reprehensible, implying the repeater is not silenced, against R' Zeira's equation with 'modim, modim'

moves.cueHe: מגונה הוא דהוי, שתוקי לא משתקינן ליה
moves.summary: infers from 'reprehensible' that he is not silenced
moves.about: the baraita: one who recites Shema and repeats it is reprehensible

moves.cueHe: לא קשיא: הא, דאמר מילתא מילתא ותני לה
moves.summary: no contradiction: the baraita speaks of repeating each word, R' Zeira of repeating each verse
moves.about: the baraita speaks of one who repeats each word (merely reprehensible); R' Zeira of one who repeats each verse (silenced)

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב פפא לאביי: ודילמא מעיקרא לא כוון דעתיה
moves.summary: Rav Pappa to Abaye: perhaps the repeater lacked intent at first and focused the second time — why silence him?
moves.about: whether one who repeats a verse of Shema must be silenced — perhaps he simply lacked intent the first time and focused the second, so it need not look like two authorities

moves.summary: Abaye: there is no familiarity with Heaven; one who lacked intent is beaten with a smith's hammer until he focuses (the 'אמר ליה' header sits on 33b.31)
moves.about: there is no casual familiarity with Heaven; one who lacked intent at first is beaten with a smith's hammer until he focuses, not permitted to repeat
